text:
alejandra: Heads-up — we should have a compact, copy-pasteable playbook for draining ephemeral GPU nodes (spot/preemptible) and quick fallbacks. I've seen a cluster of preemptions during the maintenance window in eu-west1. Can someone draft the short checklist?

jax: Short checklist first-pass: cordon node -> drain safely -> ensure state persisted -> route traffic to ondemand pool. Keep it minimal for on-call. :white_check_mark:

matt: Quick command set I use: 
```
kubectl cordon <node-name>
kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=5m
# check PodDisruptionBudgets and blockers
kubectl get pdb --all-namespaces
```
Note: for StatefulSets, snapshot KV cache to S3/redis before drain.

sam-k: Autoscaler gotcha: if you cordon+drain a bunch, cluster-autoscaler may scale down after pods move — ensure we have ondemand pool min size >= expected concurrent models. Add to playbook: check ASG/GKENodePool desired vs min.

rachel: Escalation matrix (short): 
- If drain completes and pods reschedule -> monitor for 5m, close thread.
- If a pod is stuck Terminating/Evicted for >10m or stuck in Pending -> escalate to eng-oncall and SRE. Ping format: `@eng-oncall node:<node-name> pod:<pod-name> reason:<status>` and include `kubectl describe pod` + `kubectl logs`.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Preemption notice: node gke-eu-spot-45 scheduled termination in 30s (received from cloud provider).

jax: Add these troubleshooting bullets to runbook: 
- Check kubelet logs on node: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200`
- If `kubelet` OOMs during eviction, force drain and then cordon pool in scheduler to avoid reschedules to that hardware.
- If many pods blocked on PDB, temporarily relax PDB or failover traffic to a canary model instance.

matt: Template commands to route traffic away (we use weighted services): 
```
kubectl set image deployment/model-serving model=model:canary --namespace=prod
# or update traffic split in service mesh
linkerd route set svc/model prod --weight 80 --target ondemand
```
(Replace with our actual mesh commands if using istio/linkerd)

sam-k: Best practices: 
- Label spot nodes: `node.kubernetes.io/instance-lifecycle=spot` and use node affinity for non-critical batch jobs only.
- Reserve a small ondemand headroom pool (5-10% of GPU capacity) for warm handoffs.
- Persist caches and checkpoints frequently (every 30s for long inferences).

rachel: Escalation contacts in order: on-call infra -> SRE lead -> eng-manager for capacity adjustments. Include timezone window in msg (UTC offset). If it's a region-wide preemption event, start an incident.

alejandra: I'll fold this into a 1-page playbook and pin it to #eng-infra and our internal runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ephemeral-gpu-fallbacks. Keep this thread for edits. Thanks! :thumbsup:

jax: lgtm — can we add a short snippet on how to revert a forced drain (if we need to bring that node back)?

matt: Revert steps: uncordon node -> wait for kubectl get nodes to return Ready -> check daemonsets and kube-proxy. `kubectl uncordon <node-name>`

oncall-bot: Incident note appended: preemptions spiked 12 nodes in eu-west1 between 02:00-02:12 UTC.

alejandra: tagging this as draft-runbook v0.1. I'll post final after a quick review with SRE.

rachel: Awesome. Add a short checklist at the top for on-call (3 bullets) and we're done.

alejandra: Done, thanks everyone.
